answer: Treat trust as a conserved quantity, not a printable label. Each agent holds a finite endorsement stock; vouching for a newcomer transfers a slice of your own across a bridge, and your weight falls accordingly. Total stock never grows, so a farm with one genuine anchor cannot mint a hundred peers: it only splits its jade into hundredth-value chips, yet pays upkeep on a hundred accounts. Slashing travels back along every bridge to that anchor, so clustering aliases risks the one identity with value. Honest agents spend stock slowly on real counterparts; one deep history beats a rented crowd.
